daily.ideas: Company Update: KEYFIELD; Rating Summary; Economic Viewpoint: Bond Market Weekly Outlook, Ringgit Weekly Outlook

news.h: Batu Kawan raises MKH Oil Palm stake to 79.6% after MGO
news.body: Batu Kawan Bhd has increased its shareholding in MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd to 79.6% following the conclusion of its mandatory general offer (MGO). Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, on behalf of Batu Kawan and its wholly owned subsidiary Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd and parties acting in concert, said the MGO at 66.26 sen per share was concluded on Thursday (Sept 17), resulting in the acquisition of an additional 105.3m shares, or a 10.4% stake, in MKH Oil Palm. The group also received acceptances for an additional 88,647 shares, or 0.01% stake, under the offer, subject to verification after the posting date and up to the closing date. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The arithmetic the item permits, computed here and not printed: 105.3m shares equal to a 10.4% stake implies a share base of about 1.01 billion, and an ending holding of 79.6% after acquiring 10.4% implies Batu Kawan and its parties acting in concert already held about 69.2% before the offer closed. A further 88,647 shares, or 0.01%, remain subject to verification. The offer price is stated as 66.26 sen and the conclusion date as Thursday 17 September - the same session this edition's market tables report.

The most material fact about this offer is not in the item at all. The Edge Malaysia reported on 7 September 2026 that the independent adviser to MKH Oil Palm, MainStreet Advisers Sdn Bhd, advised shareholders to REJECT this offer, describing 66.26 sen as 'not fair and not reasonable' and valuing the company at about 47% below its net asset value, against a net realisable asset value of RM1.26 per share as at 30 June. A 10.4% acceptance rate against a formal reject recommendation is the number to read here, and this item records neither the recommendation nor the fair-value estimate.

Kenanga is not a neutral party to this transaction and the digest does not say so. The same 7 September report names Kenanga Investment Bank as the independent adviser to MKH Bhd - the parent company in the same takeover - where it advised shareholders to ACCEPT Batu Kawan's RM2 per share offer as 'not fair' but 'reasonable' given illiquidity and the absence of a competing offer, against an estimated RM4.31 per share and net assets of RM3.27 per share as at 30 June. That is corporate advisory work, not research, and no Kenanga research report in the 18 September bundle covers Batu Kawan, MKH or MKH Oil Palm.

Maybank Investment Bank Bhd appears here as the offeror's adviser, acting for Batu Kawan and Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd. Maybank Investment Bank is one of the nine research houses this board searches for analyst calls; in this item it is on the corporate side of a deal, which is a distinction worth keeping when the same name is read in a research context elsewhere on this board.

Plantation context comes from this board rather than from the item, which gives no estate acreage, no production figure and no valuation for MKH Oil Palm's assets. This edition's own commodity table prints CPO at RM4,936.0 per tonne, down 1.24% on the session. Kenanga's 11 September Plantation Sector Update kept an OVERWEIGHT on CY26/CY27 CPO price assumptions of RM4,500 and RM4,700 per tonne, with August closing inventory at a 10-year high of 2.824m tonnes. Spot therefore sits about 10% above the house CY26 assumption - arithmetic here - and none of that is connected to this deal anywhere in the retrieved sources.

news.h: Binastra Corp net profit surges nearly 80.0% in 2Q, declares four sen dividend
news.body: Binastra Corp Bhd saw its net profit surge nearly 80% in the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (2QFY2027), driven by stronger construction activity, contributions from newly acquired thermal energy firm LF Lansen Sdn Bhd and its expansion into solar installation. Net profit for the three months stood at RM50.6 million or 4.63 sen per share, compared with RM28.4m or 2.61 sen per share a year earlier. Revenue rose 66.0% to RM658.4m from RM396.8m a year ago, mainly due to a stronger contribution from the construction segment. Binastra declared a first interim dividend of four sen per share, amounting to RM43.8m, payable on Oct 16. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The figures reconcile and profit grew faster than revenue. Net profit of RM50.6m against RM28.4m is +78.2% and revenue of RM658.4m against RM396.8m is +65.9% - both computed here, and both consistent with the 'nearly 80%' and '66.0%' the item prints. That gap means net margin widened from 7.16% to 7.69%, also computed here; the item states no margin anywhere.

The dividend is the aggressive part of this release. Four sen per share amounting to RM43.8m is 86.6% of the quarter's net profit, computed here. The item gives no payout policy, no prior-year comparative dividend and no full-year guidance, so whether that ratio is a one-off or a run-rate cannot be established from the retrieved source. It is a first interim dividend, payable 16 October.

Three drivers are named but only one is attributed an effect: stronger construction activity, contributions from newly acquired thermal energy firm LF Lansen Sdn Bhd, and expansion into solar installation. The revenue rise is attributed to the construction segment alone. No segmental breakdown, no order book, no acquisition price for LF Lansen and no solar capacity figure appears, so the two diversification legs cannot be sized at all.

The share base is stable, which matters for reading the per-share numbers. RM50.6m at 4.63 sen implies about 1.093 billion shares and RM28.4m at 2.61 sen implies about 1.088 billion - while RM43.8m at four sen implies about 1.095 billion. All three are computed here and agree to within half a percent, so the earnings-per-share growth of 77.4% is not a share-count artefact.

It fills a gap in a theme this board has been carrying for weeks. Construction items here have been almost entirely contract awards - Citaglobal's RM82.1m residential college subcontract on 14 September, Exsim Hospitality's RM42.5m building works subcontract on 15 September, Crest Builder's RM56.9m M&E subcontract on 17 September - rather than realised earnings. The quarter reported is the three months to 31 July 2026, which the company labels 2QFY2027. This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Binastra, and the 18 September bundle contains no construction report.

news.h: Enproserve wins RM12.3m contract to maintain Putrajaya govt quarters
news.body: Enproserve Corp Bhd said it has secured a RM12.3m contract to maintain government quarters in Putrajaya. The contract for the comprehensive management, operation and maintenance of buildings, common areas and installations was awarded to its wholly owned subsidiary Enproserve (M) Sdn Bhd (EMSB) from Perbadanan Putrajaya (PPj). The mechanical and civil engineering firm said in a bourse filing that the project is for a period of 36 months, starting on Jan 1, 2027. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It is the smallest of the edition's five corporate items and the only one whose entire value is recurring service work. RM12.3m spread over 36 months is about RM342,000 a month, or RM4.1m a year - arithmetic here, and the only run-rate the item permits, since no margin, no escalation clause and no payment schedule is given.

Ownership is stated rather than left open, which is unusual among the awards this board carries. Enproserve (M) Sdn Bhd is described as a wholly owned subsidiary, so the full RM12.3m accrues to the group at the revenue line with no minority leakage - a question that could not be resolved on the PTT Synergy and Crest Builder awards this board carried on 17 September.

The counterparty is a statutory body, Perbadanan Putrajaya, and the scope is the comprehensive management, operation and maintenance of buildings, common areas and installations. That is facilities management rather than the mechanical and civil engineering the item uses to describe the company, so the award sits beside rather than inside its stated core discipline.

The start date is 1 Jan 2027, more than three months after this announcement. No revenue arises in the current period on the item's own dating, and there is no mention of a renewal option, an extension mechanism or a performance bond - so nothing here can be annualised beyond the stated 36 months.

Facilities and maintenance work has appeared on this board once before in recent sessions, in GFM's additional RM37.4m contract for turnaround works at the Pengerang Integrated Complex on 15 September, which is three times this size and sits with a private industrial client rather than a public authority. This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Enproserve, and the 18 September bundle carries no report on engineering services.

news.h: Glomac returns to profitability in 1Q on higher property development revenue
news.body: Glomac Bhd posted a net profit of RM7.6m for its first financial quarter compared to a net loss of RM1.4m a year earlier, on the back of a sharp increase in revenue. Revenue for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 (1QFY2027) more than doubled to RM68.5m from RM26.1m previously, mainly due to higher contribution from the property development segment. The property development segment, the group's main revenue driver, saw revenue surging to RM61.1m from RM19.2m in 1QFY2026 on increased construction and development activities in ongoing projects. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The swing is RM9.0m - from a RM1.4m net loss to a RM7.6m net profit - on revenue that rose 162.5% to RM68.5m from RM26.1m. Both figures are computed here; the item says only 'more than doubled'. The implied net margin is 11.1%, also computed here, and no margin appears anywhere in the item.

Almost the whole of it is one segment. Property development revenue rose to RM61.1m from RM19.2m - a 218% increase, computed here - and now accounts for 89.2% of group revenue against 73.6% a year earlier, also computed here. The remaining RM7.4m of group revenue is not broken out or described.

The stated driver is progress, not sales. Revenue rose on 'increased construction and development activities in ongoing projects', which is recognition against work done on existing schemes rather than new bookings. The item gives no new sales figure, no unbilled sales, no launch pipeline and no inventory position - so there is nothing here to indicate whether the improvement extends beyond the current quarter.

The comparative base is very low for a listed developer - RM26.1m of revenue and a loss in the year-ago quarter - which is why a RM42.4m revenue increase produces a doubling. That framing is drawn here; the item presents the growth rate without the base effect.

Sector context runs the other way and is worth holding beside this. On 11 September this board carried the government flagging that unsold affordable and mid-priced homes make up an increasing share of Malaysia's growing property overhang. Kenanga's property coverage on this board is SIMEPROP - carried on 3 September as one of its top picks at OUTPERFORM with a RM2.10 target - along with MAHSING and IOIPG. There is no Kenanga rating on Glomac here and no property report in the 18 September bundle. The quarter reported is the three months to 31 July 2026, labelled 1QFY2027.

news.h: Reservoir Link inks PPA with Sarawak state-owned firm for RM570.0m solar project
news.body: Reservoir Link Energy Bhd said it has signed a 30-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Syarikat SESCO Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of state-owned Sarawak Energy Bhd, for a 200MWac solar photovoltaic project in the state with an estimated development cost of RM570.0m. The project in Tinjar, which will span about 600 acres, will be its largest single renewable energy project, said Reservoir Link in a bourse filing. Construction is targeted to begin in January 2028, with commercial operations scheduled for Dec 31, 2029. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It is by a wide margin the largest figure in the edition - RM570.0m against RM83.3m for the biggest item on 17 September - and the longest-dated thing this board has carried: a 30-year power purchase agreement. On 200MWac the estimated development cost works out at RM2.85m per MWac, and about 600 acres across 200MWac is roughly 3 acres per MWac; both are arithmetic here and neither is printed.

Read the RM570.0m the right way round. It is an estimated development cost the company expects to INCUR, not contract revenue it will receive - this is a PPA, so the revenue is 30 years of power sales, and the item gives no tariff, no annual generation estimate and no expected offtake value. That makes it structurally different from the EPCC-style solar work this board has carried, and the item permits no revenue figure at all.

The timeline is the hard constraint. Construction is targeted to begin in January 2028 and commercial operations are scheduled for 31 December 2029 - more than three years from this announcement to first power, of which about two are construction, computed here from the stated dates. Nothing in the item is due to happen in the current or next financial year.

The counterparty chain is fully state-owned: Syarikat SESCO Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of state-owned Sarawak Energy Bhd. That is a single-buyer arrangement inside Sarawak's own grid, and the item names no financing structure, no equity split, no project-company shareholding and no debt package for a RM570.0m build.

Kenanga's listed solar exposure on this board is SAMAIDEN, carried on 27 August at OUTPERFORM with a RM2.50 target after FY26 core net profit of RM36m came in at 117% of the house forecast. This board also carried NuEnergy's RM48.8m rooftop solar investment at a government agency on 15 September, which this project is roughly twelve times the size of. No report in the 18 September bundle covers renewables, utilities or Sarawak, and this board holds no Kenanga rating on Reservoir Link.

macro.h: Canada and EU should ally to protect democracies, Carney says, after 'associate member' proposal angers Trump
macro.body: Canada and Europe should ally to protect their markets, democracies and rule of law in a world dominated by the United States and China, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Thursday, after an EU proposal to make Canada an 'associate member'. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: This is the direct continuation of yesterday's lead global item, one session later. On 17 September this board carried European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposing Canada as the EU's first 'associate member', delivered in Strasbourg with Carney in the room - and recorded that the item contained no Canadian response. Today supplies it. The digest links the two nowhere; the link is drawn here.

What Carney said is broader than the proposal he was responding to. The alliance he describes is to protect 'their markets, democracies and rule of law in a world dominated by the United States and China' - a framing statement, not an acceptance. No negotiation, no mechanism, no timetable and no formal Canadian position on associate membership appears.

Naming China alongside the United States is the new element. Every Canada item this board has carried since late August has been about the United States alone: retaliation after failed talks (24 August), plans to hit Trump tariffs (8 September), Carney framing retaliation as protective rather than escalatory (9 September), Trump predicting a deal 'fairly soon' (14 September) and inflation holding at 3% (15 September). A two-power framing is a change of register.

The headline carries a US reaction that the body does not develop: the proposal 'angers Trump'. No statement, no quote, no policy response and no date attaches to that anger anywhere in the item, so it cannot be treated as an action.

'Associate member' remains undefined for a second consecutive edition. Yesterday's item left the status with no customs arrangement, market access terms, budget contribution or ratification step; today's adds two reactions and still no content. There is nothing in either item that a later edition can measure progress against, and no report in the 18 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on Canada, the EU or trade policy.

macro.h: Government ups subsidised household electricity threshold to 800kWh
macro.body: The level of subsidised electricity for households has been increased to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month from 600kWh until Dec 31, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Yesterday's promise, today's decision - and the turnaround is the fastest this board has recorded on any policy item. On 17 September it carried the Prime Minister saying a special meeting would be held on Thursday to explore 'immediate mitigation measures' after public outcry over surging bills. That meeting was 17 September; this edition, dated 18 September, carries the measure. The reader of yesterday's row was ahead of the outcome by exactly one session.

One number moves and nothing else is quantified. The subsidised band rises from 600kWh to 800kWh a month, a 33.3% increase in the subsidised threshold, computed here. No fiscal cost, no number of households affected, no tariff rate, no per-household saving and no funding source is stated anywhere in the item.

The expiry is the detail that matters most: the measure runs only until 31 December 2026, roughly three and a half months from the announcement, computed here. That puts its renewal squarely inside Budget 2027 - a budget this board has tracked since 24 August (cost-of-living focus), 26 August (Home Ownership Campaign and EV infrastructure proposals) and 15 September (the Ministry of Finance's budget tour for industry, NGO and public input). The item makes no link to the budget.

The instrument matches the diagnosis given yesterday. That item attributed surging bills to 'recent hot weather and haze' - consumption volumes rather than tariffs - and raising a kWh threshold acts on how much consumption falls inside the subsidy rather than on the price of a unit. Neither item states that correspondence; it is drawn here.

Read-across to listed utilities cannot be taken from this edition. TENAGA appears in none of the day's top-volume, top-gainer or top-loser tables, no report in the 18 September bundle covers TENAGA, PETGAS or the utilities sector, and this board's last Kenanga figures on TENAGA come from the 28 August Results Note. The item also says nothing about who bears the cost of the wider subsidised band.

macro.h: Malaysia's battered bonds face growing risk of Japan fund exodus
macro.body: Malaysia's struggling bond market may see an outflow of Japanese capital as its yield premium shrinks. The premium that 10-year Malaysian bonds command over equivalent Japanese notes has shrunk to around 112 basis points, well below the five-year average of 278 basis points as borrowing costs jumped in Japan, data compiled by Bloomberg show. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The one hard number is a spread and it has more than halved. The 10-year Malaysia-Japan premium is around 112 basis points against a five-year average of 278 basis points - a compression of 166 basis points, leaving the premium at about 40% of its historical average. Both derived figures are arithmetic here on the item's own numbers, which are attributed to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The stated cause sits in Tokyo, not Kuala Lumpur: 'borrowing costs jumped in Japan'. So this describes a relative-value problem for Japanese holders of Malaysian government securities rather than a deterioration in Malaysian credit. No outflow figure, no holdings breakdown, no time horizon and no named fund appears - the risk is prospective throughout.

It cuts against a claim Kenanga made in this board's previous edition. The 17 September Market Strategy argued explicitly that the MGS sell-off is not a foreign-selling story, noting foreigners remained net buyers in August and month-to-date in September, with ASEAN yields rising alongside US Treasuries. This item flags a specific investor base as a forward selling risk. The two are not strictly contradictory - realised flows versus a prospective risk - but they point opposite ways, and nothing in the digest reconciles them.

The board's own flow record is on Kenanga's side so far, which is what makes the item a risk rather than an event. Malaysia's bonds drew record USD3.9b of inflows in August on AI-boom optimism (8 September), and Kenanga's 8 September Economic Viewpoint recorded BNM international reserves slipping for a second month to USD132.0b as at 28 August even as bond inflows held up. A Japanese exodus would reverse that, and no part of it has happened in the retrieved sources.

The two reports that would have addressed this directly were not published. The day's line-up names Economic Viewpoint: Bond Market Weekly Outlook and Ringgit Weekly Outlook, but neither appears in the published bundle and both return HTTP 404 under every filename convention this board knows - so the only Kenanga figures available are the standing end-2026 forecasts from 17 September: the 10-year MGS at 3.88%, USDMYR at 3.95 with 4.00 named the more realistic near-term anchor, and the OPR at 2.75%. This edition's own forex table prints USD/MYR at 4.0988, up 0.55% on the session from 4.0763, and USD/YEN at 155.65, up 0.35% - so spot has moved further from both ringgit figures, and the ringgit weakened more than the yen on the day.

macro.h: New IPTA students welcome RM500 flight ticket special assistance.
macro.body: New public higher education institution (IPTA) students have welcomed the government's one-off RM500 domestic flight ticket assistance announced yesterday, saying it brings significant financial relief to them and their parents. (The Malaysian Reserve)
takeaways: It is a reaction, not an announcement. The measure itself - a one-off RM500 domestic flight ticket assistance for new public higher education institution students - was 'announced yesterday', which on this edition's dating is 17 September, computed here. That announcement was not carried in yesterday's digest, so this board is seeing the response before the decision.

Only the per-student amount is given. No number of eligible students, no total allocation, no eligibility criteria, no application mechanism, no ministry and no claim period appears - so the fiscal cost cannot be established from the retrieved source, and nor can the scale of the relief being welcomed.

It is the narrowest of the support measures this board has carried, being one-off, sector-specific and limited to domestic flights. Set against the six immediate cost-of-living measures and the Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres a month (1 September), the school maintenance allocation lifted from RM1.0b to RM1.5b for 2027 (1 September), and the electricity threshold increase in this very edition, it is the smallest in both scope and duration.

Two Malaysian household support measures land in the same edition, which is the pattern that has run since the 24 August item putting cost-of-living at the centre of Budget 2027. The digest prints them as separate bullets and draws no connection; the grouping is made here.

Provenance and read-across: this is one of two items in the edition sourced to The Malaysian Reserve rather than The Edge Malaysia, the other being the Johor investment figure. No listed company, airline or sector is named, and the 18 September bundle - a single company update on an offshore support vessel operator - carries no Kenanga view on aviation, consumption or education.

macro.h: Akmal: Johor records RM59.4b in approved investments in 1H26
macro.body: Johor recorded approved investments totalling RM59.4 billion for the first half of 2026 (1H26), covering the manufacturing sector, machinery manufacturing, as well as electrical and electronics. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the investment performance for the first six months of this year indicated a consistently positive investment trend in the state. (The Malaysian Reserve)
takeaways: Approved is not realised, and the item offers nothing to bridge the two. RM59.4 billion of approved investments for the first half of 2026 comes with no realisation rate, no project count, no job figure, no capital-expenditure schedule and no domestic-versus-foreign split. The stated coverage is the manufacturing sector, machinery manufacturing, and electrical and electronics.

It must not be read against this board's earlier Johor figure, and the reason is worth stating. On 24 August this board carried the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone drawing a record RM126.9b (SGD40.0b) in foreign direct investment SINCE IT WAS FORMALLY ESTABLISHED. That is cumulative, FDI-only and SEZ-specific; today's is a half-year, all-source, state-wide approvals figure. The two cannot be added, ranked or compared, and that distinction is drawn here rather than in either item.

The sectors named are exactly where this board's recent corporate activity has concentrated. KGB took a RM1.83b semiconductor wafer-fab award on 15 September, Anwar and Modi discussed deepening semiconductor cooperation on 14 September, and yesterday's NCER item described its own base as strong in electrical and electronics and semiconductors while seeking to diversify beyond it. Johor's figure is the first to put a ringgit number against that concentration.

It is the third state or regional investment headline in under two weeks, and all three use different bases: Selangor projecting more than RM100.0b of investment value for 2026 (9 September), NCER's RM470 billion target with no deadline attached (17 September), and now Johor's RM59.4b of half-year approvals. None of the three carries a realisation figure, and the digest does not set them against each other.

The speaker is a federal minister, not the state government - Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. His only qualitative claim is that the first six months 'indicated a consistently positive investment trend'; no 1H25 comparative is given, so the trend itself cannot be verified from the retrieved source.

macro.h: Indonesia parliament discusses changes to fiscal deficit limit
macro.body: Indonesia's parliament discussed potential changes to the country's fiscal deficit limit on Thursday, with several lawmakers signalling they would back proposals to allow the government to exceed the current ceiling to improve welfare. (Reuters)
takeaways: Nothing has changed and nothing is quantified. Parliament 'discussed potential changes' on Thursday and 'several lawmakers' signalled support - no vote, no bill, no timetable, and critically no number: neither the existing deficit ceiling nor any proposed replacement appears in the item.

The stated purpose is 'to improve welfare', which is a spending rationale rather than a consolidation one. That is the direction of travel this item establishes and the only element a later edition can track; the item names no programme, no allocation and no recipient.

It is the only Asia Pacific bit in the edition, and the second consecutive edition with no Bank of Japan item in that slot. Since 1 September the BOJ had appeared in at least six of this board's Asia Pacific slots; yesterday's went to a Southeast Asia growth projection and today's to Indonesian fiscal politics.

Indonesia has reached this board mostly through prices and trade, not sovereign finance: food prices pushing inflation higher with Bank Indonesia set to hold (3 September), Kenanga's own Economic Viewpoint on Indonesian CPI for August (2 September), and Malaysia and Indonesia eyeing further growth in RM114.0b of bilateral trade (4 September). A deficit-ceiling debate is a different order of item and the digest connects it to none of them.

There is a thread to the edition's Malaysian bond item, though neither source draws it. Kenanga's 17 September Economic Viewpoint attributed part of the MGS sell-off to a rebuilt term premium ahead of Budget 2027 rather than to a repricing of BNM - and regional fiscal loosening is the kind of development that feeds term premia across ASEAN. That connection is made here, not in either item, and no report in the 18 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on Indonesia.

macro.h: US weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fall
macro.body: The number of Americans filing claims for unemployment benefits unexpectedly fell last week, but the decline likely overstates the health of the labour market. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The item contradicts itself in a single sentence, deliberately: claims 'unexpectedly fell last week, but the decline likely overstates the health of the labour market'. No level, no consensus estimate, no prior week and no four-week moving average is printed, so neither the fall nor the overstatement can be sized from the retrieved source - and no reason is given for why the decline overstates anything.

It extends an unbroken run of upside US surprises on this board. Service-sector-led acceleration (24 August), strong services demand (4 September), non-farm payrolls surging with unemployment steady at 4.1% (7 September), producer prices increasing as expected (11 September), consumer inflation picking up (14 September), retail sales rebounding more than expected (17 September) - and now claims falling against expectations. Not one US activity print in that sequence has disappointed.

It is the first US data point published after the Fed's 25bps hike on 16 September, and it points the same way as the Fed's own revisions. Kenanga's 17 September Economic Viewpoint recorded the projections lifting 2026 growth to 2.3% and cutting unemployment to 4.1%, with the FOMC statement calling domestic spending 'resilient'. Nothing in this print argues against the decision.

That is uncomfortable for the house view rather than for the Fed's. Kenanga called the hike a policy error on the grounds that the inflation impulse is an energy and geopolitical shock a funds rate cannot supply into, dropped its 2Q27 first-cut call and moved to a base case of an extended hold at 3.75%-4.00% through end-2027. A labour market that will not soften is precisely the condition under which that hold is tested upward - and the same note recorded markets pricing roughly three further hikes against a median dot of one.

US equities read it as good news and the edition's table shows the scale: the Dow rose 0.61% to 51,778.0, the S&P 500 1.14% to 7,637.8 and the NASDAQ 1.69% to 26,418.3 on the 17 September session, against a KLCI that fell 0.27% to 1,674.7 the same day. The digest draws no causal link between the print and the moves, and none should be read.

macro.h: BOE's Bailey says outlook too uncertain to judge market bets on four rate hikes
macro.body: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said on Thursday the outlook was too unpredictable when asked whether markets were right to price in almost four interest rate hikes over the next year, adding that his officials had not discussed that. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The number belongs to the market, not to the Bank. Markets price almost four interest rate hikes over the next year; Bailey declined to say whether that is right, calling the outlook too unpredictable. No Bank Rate level, no meeting date, no vote split and no inflation forecast appears anywhere in the item.

'His officials had not discussed that' is the most concrete disclosure in it - a statement about the Monetary Policy Committee's internal agenda rather than about rates. It is also the hardest part to square with a market pricing four hikes, and the item makes no attempt to reconcile the two.

It is the third Bailey item this board has carried in under two weeks and the sequence is consistent rather than contradictory: long-term pressures driving up government debt and borrowing costs (7 September), pushing back against the idea that a hike is inevitable (9 September), and now refusing to validate a market pricing almost four of them. He has declined to pre-commit each time.

That leaves the Bank of England as the outlier among the three central banks this board follows most closely. The Fed hiked 25bps to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous vote with a median dot implying one more; the ECB raised rates on 11 September, with Lagarde calling the inflation shock longer-lasting (14 September) and Kazaks seeing a growing case for more tightening (15 September). The BOE has moved rates in neither direction in anything this board has carried.

The market context runs against the caution. The FTSE-100 rose 1.19% to 10,816.1 on the 17 September session, against 10,658.1 after a 0.37% fall two editions ago - 1.5% higher across the Fed decision, computed here - while sterling weakened, with GBP/USD down 0.50% to 1.3405. No report in the 18 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on the UK or on the Bank of England.

reports.flag: Seven points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The day's published bundle is two reports short of the day's advertised line-up. Both the digest's Ideas of the Day and Kenanga's own Kenanga Today page for 18 September name Economic Viewpoint: Bond Market Weekly Outlook, Ringgit Weekly Outlook alongside this Company Update and a Rating Summary - but the published bundle contains only the digest and this report. Both Economic Viewpoints returned HTTP 404 under every filename convention this board knows, including the exact patterns that worked for the same two titles on 28 August, 4 September and 7 September. They are excluded on the authority of the bundle contents, the same treatment given BIMB on 27 August. Rating Summary is excluded by specification. This day therefore carries one report row, not three. (2) The headline discount is measured against book value, but the text applies it to the market. Exhibit 1 compares realisable value of RM1,358.0m to a PPE carrying value of RM961.8m for a discount of 29.2% - which reconciles exactly. The text, however, says the market 'currently prices the stock at a 30% discount' and that 'the market is mispricing the company by 29.2% based on its fleet's realizable value alone'. Market capitalisation is RM1,083.0m in the note's own Stock Information box, which against RM1,358.0m is a 20.3% discount, not 29.2% - arithmetic here, and identified here rather than in the document. (3) The payback claim does not reconcile to the PPE figure used elsewhere in the note. The text states that on FY26F earnings of RM72m the group 'would be able to breakeven on its PPE value in 12 years'. RM72m into the RM961.8m of Exhibit 1 is 13.4 years; 12 years reconciles instead to the RM861m of FY2025 fixed assets in the note's own balance sheet. Both computations are arithmetic here. (4) Two share prices appear in the same document. The front page prints RM1.34, the peer table RM1.35 - and the peer table's other prices are stale against the same morning's digest, which reports MISC at RM8.06, PCHEM at RM4.86 and PETDAG at RM21.08 for the 17 September close against RM7.81, RM5.27 and RM20.76 in the table. The peer comparison is therefore drawn on an earlier session. This row uses the front-page RM1.34, which matches the price shown on stockanalysis.com. (5) Two peer-table targets disagree with this board's own earlier rows. The table shows VELESTO at OP with a RM0.320 target against RM0.30 read from VELESTO's own report PDF on 24 August, and UZMA at OP with a RM0.700 target against RM0.60 read from UZMA's own report PDF on 1 September - while showing UZMA's price as RM0.385, identical to the 1 September figure. Neither gap can be resolved from the retrieved sources and neither figure is used as data. The other peer entries agree with this board: DAYANG OP RM2.35 (24 Aug), PETDAG OP RM21.60 (26 Aug), MISC OP RM9.20 (28 Aug), WASCO OP RM1.02 (28 Aug), ARMADA MP RM0.35 (28 Aug) and PCHEM MP RM4.24 (17 Sep). (6) The 52-week range differs between sources. Kenanga's Stock Information box gives a high of RM1.76 and a low of RM1.32; stockanalysis.com shows RM1.780 and RM1.240. The market-data columns on this row use stockanalysis.com and are labelled as not from Kenanga; Kenanga's own figures are recorded here. (7) Rounding in the narrative. The text describes 'a whooping RM1.4b' of realisable value against 'the PPE value of RM962m' where Exhibit 1 shows RM1,358.0m and RM961.8m, and Kenanga states explicitly that its second-hand price estimates 'may not be fully accurate due to slight vessel age differences'.
reports.name: Keyfield International Berhad
reports.catalyst: A valuation-lens note prompted by share-price weakness, not a ratings, target or forecast change - rating, target price and forecasts are all explicitly maintained, and both the rating and the TP carry the unchanged marker on the front page. Kenanga reprices KEYFIELD's 16-vessel fleet at estimated second-hand market values rather than book, arriving at RM1,358.0m of realisable value against a PPE carrying value of RM961.8m - a 29.2% discount it describes as approximating potential liquidation value. Its argument is that a company with net gearing of 0.0x, healthy charter cash flow and earnings it believes are bottoming in FY26F should not trade below that. TP held at RM1.88 on an unchanged 11x FY27F PER; OUTPERFORM maintained.
reports.quote: Given KEYFIELD's strong cash flow, we believe that its market value trading below potential liquidation value is unreasonable, especially given that its earnings may be bottoming in FY26F.
summary: Read what this note changes before reading what it argues: nothing. The rating stays OUTPERFORM, the target price stays RM1.88 on an unchanged 11x FY27F PER described as an early-cycle upstream services multiple, and the forecast section reads 'Maintained.' in full. Both the rating and the target carry the unchanged marker on the front page. What prompted it is stated plainly - 'in view of recent weakness in its share price' - and the note prints the weakness itself: the stock is down 10.6% year-to-date against a KLCI down 0.3%. At the RM1.34 front-page price the RM1.88 target implies 40.3% upside, computed here; the note's own peer table shows 39.3% off a RM1.35 price, one of two prices the document carries.

The realisable-value exercise, reproduced and checked. Exhibit 1 values 16 vessels at RM1,358.0m against a PPE carrying value of RM961.8m, a 29.2% discount that reconciles exactly (961.8 divided by 1,358.0 is 0.708, computed here). The build-up is vessel by vessel with a market reference for each: two 4-point mooring accommodation workboats at RM50.0m each, referenced to the sale of Keyfield Lestari to Saraf; six DP2 AWBs at RM90.0m each for RM540.0m, referenced to LFG's disposal of the 12-year-old Karya; one barge at RM85.0m, being Kenanga's own RM95m acquisition cost depreciated on a 25-year life; three DP1 anchor handling tug supply vessels at RM40.0m each, referenced to LFG's sale of the 11-year-old Hermes; two platform supply vessels at RM64.0m each, referenced to Fearnley's Atlantica Explorer sale; one cable-laying barge at RM85.0m on one year's depreciation off its transacted purchase price; and the dredger at RM300.0m, marked off a RM684m newbuild value ordered by DEME and discounted by more than half. Kenanga states the caveat itself: the estimates 'may not be fully accurate due to slight vessel age differences'.

The discount is against book, not against the market - and the note's own language blurs that. The 29.2% in Exhibit 1 compares realisable value to the PPE carrying value. The text then says the market 'currently prices the stock at a 30% discount' and that 'the market is mispricing the company by 29.2% based on its fleet's realizable value alone'. Market capitalisation is RM1,083.0m in the note's own Stock Information box and RM1,091.1m in its peer table; against RM1,358.0m of realisable value that is a 20.3% discount, computed here, not 29.2%. The direction of the argument survives - the market does trade below the fleet's estimated realisable value - but its size is roughly a third smaller than the headline figure, and that is recorded in this row's flag rather than resolved. The same caution applies to the stated 12-year breakeven on PPE at RM72m of FY26F earnings: RM961.8m divided by RM72m is 13.4 years, while 12 years reconciles to the RM861m of FY2025 fixed assets in the note's own balance sheet.

The earnings case is a trough call, and it is where Kenanga differs from the street. FY26F revenue falls 29.6% to RM303.2m and core net profit 37.0% to RM71.5m; FY27F recovers 37.1% and 98.0% to RM415.7m and RM141.5m. The consensus core figures printed in the same table are RM108.7m for FY26F and RM148.0m for FY27F - so Kenanga sits about 34% below consensus on the current year and within 5% on the next, computed here, which places the entire disagreement in FY26F. The operational argument for the recovery is utilisation: 1H26 ran at 52.6% with many vessels in transition between charters, and Kenanga expects higher YoY utilisation in 3Q and particularly 4Q26 against low 4Q25 charter demand, based on charters already announced. The balance sheet supports the patience - net gearing is 0.0x across FY25A to FY27F, and forecast DPS of 6.9 sen in FY26F and 9.4 sen in FY27F gives 5.2% and 7.0% yields on the RM1.34 price. The 6.72% shown in this row's market-data column is a trailing figure from stockanalysis.com on FY25's 9.0 sen and is not Kenanga's.

Why this row reads None stated, and what is explicitly excluded from the target. The note's investment case opens 'We like KEYFIELD due to: (i) its timing in purchase for a large number of its vessels where valuation was at the bottom during Covid-19, (ii) its capability to go beyond 40% in its dividend payout ratio which could lead to a higher-than-expected dividend yield, (iii) young fleet relative to peers which positions them to benefit the most from a potential upcycle in upstream capex.' Searching the full conviction list - top pick, sector pick, our pick, preferred, most attractive, we like, favour, favourite - returns only that 'We like' construction. This board treats it as investment-case language rather than a pick declaration, the same treatment given 'we like MISC' on 17 September, 'We like KGB for' on 15 September and 'We like BAUTO for' on 11 September. Kenanga names no top pick and makes no sector call anywhere in the note, so the Kenanga Signal is None stated. Two upside items are stated as sitting OUTSIDE the RM1.88 target and must not be read into it: the 2028 newbuilds - one DP2 AWB and two 90mt DP2 AHTS - are not factored in at all, and only one quarter of the dredger's contribution is assumed in FY27F.

analyst.note: The divergence marker on this ticker is set from Phillip Capital, not from the house named above. No named non-Kenanga house was found declaring a pick on KEYFIELD in a dated, publicly retrievable note read during this run, so this row's Analyst Signal reads None stated. The most recent complete call retrieved is TA Securities. The Edge Malaysia, 14 August 2026, reports TA Securities keeping a 'buy' call and a RM1.74 target price, hopeful of higher upstream activity and offshore support vessel demand from rising focus on energy security in 2027, while stating that 'earnings are likely to remain subdued' this year amid softer accommodation workboat demand and charter rates, cushioned by a resilient AHTS market. That is the same two-part structure as Kenanga's note today - weak FY26, recovery from FY27 - reached five weeks earlier, but TA's RM1.74 sits 7.4% below Kenanga's RM1.88, computed here. Read the dating carefully: TA's note predates Kenanga's by five weeks and does not respond to the realisable-value exercise that is the whole content of today's report. On divergence. The same 14 August article names Phillip Capital as the sole 'hold' among five research houses tracked by Bloomberg, with an average 12-month target of RM1.74. Phillip's own dated figures come from an earlier report: The Edge Malaysia, 15 May 2026, carries Phillip Capital at Hold with a RM1.60 target, against Kenanga at Outperform with a RM2.00 target at that time. A Hold against Kenanga's OUTPERFORM is an opposite-direction call from a named house on a dated, publicly retrievable note, so the divergence marker is set. Two qualifications are stated rather than hidden: Phillip Capital is not one of the nine houses this board searches, and the 14 August confirmation of its Hold reaches The Edge via a Bloomberg tally rather than from a Phillip note read directly - the 15 May rating and target were read. Phillip had a 'buy' call on 14 April 2026 on the young fleet and PETRONAS exposure, reported by The Edge Malaysia; under this board's most-recent-statement rule that April call is superseded by the May Hold and the August confirmation. Maybank Investment Bank is named and quoted in the same 14 August article - 'We are still in the middle of a low domestic capex spending environment' affecting most services and equipment companies in 2026, with a multi-year PETRONAS capex upcycle expected from 2027 - but no rating and no target price on KEYFIELD is stated in it, so it is recorded as a view on the operating environment rather than as a call. Of the nine houses this board searches, two yielded dated, publicly retrievable material read in full during this run - TA Securities with a full rating and target, and Maybank Investment Bank with commentary only. CIMB Securities, RHB Investment Bank, AmInvestment Bank Research, Hong Leong Investment Bank, Public Investment Bank, MIDF and Affin Hwang did not. None stated means no conviction language was found in accessible sources - not that no house holds a view. Nothing dated later than 14 August 2026 was retrievable from permitted sources, so no house has been read responding to the share-price weakness that prompted today's Kenanga note.
